territorial_scope.description: Applies within Japan, defined as the area where the Act is in force; protection of foreign works depends on nationality, first publication in Japan or treaty obligations.

summary.short: Japan's Copyright Act (1970) sets authors' and related rights in works, performances, records, broadcasts and wired broadcasts, with exceptions for private copying, information analysis, quotation and education, compulsory licensing with government approval, and compensation payments.
summary.long: The Act defines works (Art. 2) and sets authors' moral rights (Arts. 18-20) and economic rights of reproduction, performance, public transmission, distribution and translation (Arts. 21-28). It sets rights of performers, record producers, broadcasters and wired broadcasters (Arts. 89-100). Exceptions include private-use reproduction, with compensation duties on specified digital recording devices and media (Art. 30(3)), use for purposes not involving enjoyment of expression, including technology development and information analysis (Art. 30-4), library reproduction and transmission (Art. 31), quotation (Art. 32), school use (Arts. 33-35) and non-commercial performance (Art. 38). Certain uses require a licence or ruling from the Commissioner for Cultural Affairs, with deposits or compensation (Arts. 67-69), and compensation disputes go to court (Art. 72). Unauthorised copies made for other purposes are deemed reproductions (Art. 49). Protection depends on nationality or first publication in Japan or treaty membership (Art. 6). Terms run for 70 years after death or publication, with separate rules for related rights (Arts. 51-54, 101). The text provided is partial and covers Chapters 1 to 5 up to Art. 104-11.

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the title, the amending clause and Arts 1 to 104-12; it ends at the heading of Art. 104-13, whose body is in part 2. Relations are those stated in this part only. Cross-referenced instruments are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty and the citation is in target_text; treaties are named in target_text only. The text refers to later enacted laws (e.g., 2009 and 2014 acts), but no as-of date or version is stated in this part. The section_status entry is required by the schema even though relation entries are present. Part 2 covers Arts 104-13 to 104-47, Arts 113-125 (incl. penal provisions and civil remedies in Arts 112-118, enforcement in Arts 119-125), and the 附則 with its amendment history. Only cross-references stated in this part are coded. The 附則 headings list numerous amending acts from 1978 to 2026; these are not individually coded as amended_by here. The 令和二年 附則 text also contains amendment instructions to 映画の盗撮の防止に関する法律 and プログラム登録特例法, not coded here. Internal conditional numbering: Art 113(5) is read as 113(4) under 平成30 附則第八条 if an earlier commencement applies. Enforcement, definitions and obligations are not coded in this part of the annotation.
